messages:
Sam: Thinking out loud — we should reconcile the canary A/B flow with automatic fallback so user sessions don't see flapping during rollouts. ideas for a low-complexity boundary between router + rollout controller? :thinking:
Jia: +1. main constraints: stateful sessions (chat, KV cache) and keeping latency SLOs when failing back. we also need operator kill-switch.
Omar: Two options i've sketched: 1) router-only: keep routing decision deterministic per-session, router does automatic switch to fallback model on probe failures. 2) controller-driven: the rollout controller updates routing rules per-segment with TTLs and warmup hints.
Lucy: Router-only is simpler but leaks rollout logic into router. controller-driven centralizes signals but increases routing latency and requires push consistency. tradeoffs.
Priya: We also need to consider cache priming. If we flip a session to fallback, KV cache miss storms are real. we should add a small warmup window + soft-traffic shadowing.
Sam: Exactly. sketch of hybrid i like: controller computes segments + stable switchpoints, router applies sticky mapping for session_id -> variant until TTL. controller can instruct router to force-fallback if health signals cross threshold.
Jia: Love hybrid. keep failure domain narrow: per-tenant or per-route thresholds. global kills should still be possible. also probe signal types: latency p95, error-rate, and model-quality tag (from evals).
Omar: Minimal config example (proto-yaml) we used in discussion:
```
rollout_policy:
  mode: gradual
  segment_key: session_id
  initial_percent: 5
  step_interval: 10m
  failover_thresholds:
    error_rate: 0.05
    p95_latency_ms: 1200
  fallback_variant: redwood-lite-v1
  warmup_shadow: 10%
```
Lucy: note `warmup_shadow` = replicate a small fraction of traffic to new variant for cache/priming without cutting live traffic. avoids big misses.
Priya: How about session affinity corner: if a session is mid-conversation and controller forces fallback for all new sessions, do we migrate existing sessions? i'd prefer no automatic migration unless we have a session-transfer mechanism (kv snapshot of session context).
Sam: Agreed. default: no live migration. options: 1) delayed drain (let session finish, new sessions go to fallback), 2) active transfer (complex). pick delayed drain as default.
Jia: Observability hooks: controller must emit reason codes for fallbacks (e.g., health_probe:latency_high, eval_regression:drop). router should tag responses with `variant_source` and `fallback_reason` for downstream tracing.
Omar: For automatic recovery, controller should require consecutive probe windows to clear before reintroducing variant. some hysteresis to avoid oscillation.
Lucy: Ops UX: one-button rollback in console, with immediate force-route and option to preserve session leases. also a simulation mode: `--dry-run route-decisions` to preview mapping.
Priya: Security + data residency: fallback variants might live in a different region; the policy needs to allow per-route constraints to avoid crossing tenancy/regulatory boundaries.
infra-oncall: deploy-bot just posted a canary start for context: Deploy-bot: Deploy started: canary 10% -> redwood-alpha-v2 at 2026-03-19T22:13Z :rocket:
Sam: For next steps: write a one-pager describing hybrid boundary (controller responsibilities vs router responsibilities), include failure-mode diagrams and a minimal rollout policy schema. i'll volunteer to draft the one-pager.
Jia: I'll add a short eval plan for quality checks and the telemetry events we need.
Omar: I'll prototype the router sticky mapping + TTL behavior in a small PoC.
Lucy: i'll mock the console rollback flow and a dry-run toggle.
Priya: i'll validate data-residency constraints and add a config flag to opt-out of cross-region fallback.
Sam: Cool — thanks everyone. tagging @infra-oncall to watch for any canary blips while we iterate. :thumbsup:
